Michel was last seen at the Tobermory Ferry Terminal on Wednesday, September 9, 2009 at 7 a.m.  It is not known if he purchased a ticket to board the ferry. She suffered from lung disease and had severe arthritis of her lumbar spine, which may have been painful. When witnessed going over the Falls, she was wearing a long overcoat, possibly grey, and carrying a green umbrella. There is no confirmation that the jumper and the deceased are the same person, however the general descriptions are in agreement. The condition of her remains suggest that she had been in the water for weeks to months.

Case reference: 2014006317.CaseDesc: Bradden Bushie was last seen on November 16, 2013, when a group home worker dropped him off outside 300 Portage Ave. in Winnipeg, Manitoba, saying he was meeting a female friend at the library. Family and police are concerned for Bradden's well-being.

Shoes: White, Running shoes with black stripes similar to Adidas brand

Case reference: 2019053661.CaseDesc:
On July 2, 1988, an unidentified man was found in the parking lot of the Value Village
on East Hastings Street in Vancouver, British Columbia. The man had suffered from a
heart attack, and the results of his autopsy showed evidence of previous heart damage and a case of mild chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

Case reference: 2011006399.CaseDesc: Rose Mary Friday suddenly disappeared from her residence in Brampton on June 19th 1974. Her disappearance was not reported to the authorities at that time. In October of 1974 Rose Mary's husband remarried. His new wife became suspicious about the account given to her about Rose Mary and she made a Missing Person report to Peel Police. The investigation started but unfortunately the case became cold when all leads failed to find Rose Mary. The disappearance of Rose Mary is considered suspicious.

Other: Right arm paralyzed at the elbow, leaving arm permanently bent.
Scoliosis of thoracic spine, joint disease
Scar: Pelvis, No gall blader, Hysterectomy, Appendectomy, Hiatus Hernia Repair

Case reference: 2006024499.CaseDesc: Allan MacKenzie was last seen in Chapleau, Ontario on November 5, 1987. He was making a delivery with his red and green tractor/trailer to the Ministry of Natural Resources in Chapleau and then believed to be enroute to Toronto, Ontario. He was subsequently reported overdue in Toronto and has not been seen since. His trailer and tractor were located, parked north of Sultan, ON.

Case reference: 2014003618.CaseDesc: Maggie Mink was last in contact with her family in 1985; at the time, she indicated that she was moving to Vancouver from Manitoba. Ms. Mink was documented to be living in Vancouver's west end in 1987. There have been no further records of Ms. Mink since.

Case reference: 2014004044.CaseDesc: Thomas Buck left his residence in St. Catherine's, Ontario, at 9am on May 30,1993. His vehicle was later located abandoned in a parking lot in Niagara Falls, Ontario.

Case reference: 2017011306.CaseDesc: On August 31,1976, Robert and Gabriel Vanderheyden were walking on the pier in Port Stanley, Ontario when a wave crashed over them throwing Robert into the water.

Case reference: 2018062818.CaseDesc: On April 26, 1993, at approximately 1:30am, Rafat Abugazia was last seen by his roommate in Toronto, Ontario.

Case reference: 2014006991.CaseDesc: Maxime Perreault was living alone and in an isolated area in the municipality of East Bolton and was working in the municipality of Eastman, in the Eastern Townships region of Quebec. On April 28, 2014, Maxime contacted his family and friends stating that he would visit them around May 3, 2014 in Beloeil, Quebec. He never arrived. He usually travels on foot, by bike, by bus or hitchhiking with a navy blue backpack.

Case reference: 2021017120.CaseDesc: On May 2, 2021, Nathan Zuk was reported missing by family when he did not return from a boat trip. In mid-December 2020, Nathan departed from his family residence in Whaletown, British Columbia, in a 14-foot skiff rowboat. He was thought to be en route to a location near the Pryce Channel, Deer Passage and or Toba Inlet in British Columbia. Despite having left with supplies that would have lasted him for several months, Nathan had backcountry experience and would have eventually returned. Nathan had medical and some mobility issues.

Hair: Brown, Wavy, Greying at temples, may have longer hair and a beard
Jacket: Leather, Black, Black leather jacket with a grey hood (zip up style)
Other: Middle Back, Curvature in the spine causing mobility issues

Case reference: 2014005742.CaseDesc: Philip Mark Oslizlok was reported missing by his family in early 2010. He was last seen on September 2, 2009 when he went to the Vancouver Police Department to receive an employment record clearance. Mr. Oslizlok last contacted his family via email on November 20, 2009 to inform them that he had gotten a job on a cruise line and would not be returning home for Christmas. There are no records of employment for Philip at any of the cruise lines. He has not been seen or heard from since.

Case reference: 2014005768.CaseDesc: On March 16, 2012, Sol Han was seen for the last time in Toronto, Ontario. That day, Sol did not show up for school.
